Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock is 2.1% lower to trade at $165.61 this afternoon, struggling to maintain its recent bounce off the $160 area, and still sporting a 6.5% year-to-date deficit. Despite brushing off its upbeat Q3, the software giant's rebound could be set to resume, with a bull signal now flashing.

Per Schaeffer's Senior Quantitative Analyst Rocky White, Palantir stock has traded within 0.75 times the 100-day moving average's 20-day average true range (ATR), after spending at least 80% of the previous two weeks and 80% of the prior 42 trading sessions above the trendline.

This setup has occurred five other times over the last decade, after which the stock was higher one month later every time, averaging a 5.3% gain. From its current perch, a shift of this magnitude would put PLTR back just shy of $175.

Bearish attention could be due for an unwind. This is per Schaeffer's put/call open interest ratio (SOIR) of 1.12, which sits in the 91st percentile of its annual range, suggesting short-term option players have rarely been more put-heavy during the past 12 months.

Options are looking affordable as well. This is per PLTR's Schaeffer's Volatility Index (SVI) of 55%, which stands higher than just 34% of all other readings from the past year.

title: Midterm Meltdowns: 3 Top Tech Stocks Down Big Since the Election Results

Midterm Meltdowns: 3 Top Tech Stocks Down Big Since the Election Results
David Jagielski, CPA, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:22 AM MST 5 min read
NVDA
MU
PLTR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Last week, the midterm elections shook up the markets. Many stocks have been falling since the news hit that the Democratic Party would be taking control of Congress. It's created uncertainty about how strong demand will be for data centers and whether there will be a slowdown in the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out that's been a boom for many tech businesses.

Three top tech stocks that have been falling sharply of late include Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), and Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR). Are these stocks worth buying on the dip?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Nvidia

A slowdown in AI spending could make Nvidia one of the most vulnerable stocks to own, as its AI chips are seen as essential for many companies investing in the latest opportunities in tech. Just prior to the midterms, Nvidia's stock was trading at over $206. But on Tuesday, it fell to below $170 -- a level it hasn't been at since March.

Nvidia's problems, however, aren't all due to the midterms. CEO Jensen Huang has been making news for all the wrong reasons of late, reportedly being involved in a romantic relationship with a Chinese spy. The company has launched its own investigation, and it begs the question of whether Huang will stay on as CEO.

There are now tremendous question marks around Nvidia, but ultimately, none of the recent developments likely change any of the company's impressive fundamentals. As long as there isn't a full-blown reduction in AI spending, which doesn't appear probable at this stage, the company is likely going to generate strong growth for the foreseeable future.

At just 21 times trailing earnings, Nvidia's looking like a bargain buy, and the stock may be too good to pass up at its current valuation.

Micron

Micron's stock was trading at over $855 on the eve of the midterms, and last week it fell below $700. While it's bounced back from those lows, it's still not far from those levels now.

In Micron's case, it's a much riskier stock to own than Nvidia, simply because so much of the bull case hinges on there being a continued shortage of memory and storage products. If there are any signs of that coming to an end, such as slowing demand for AI-related infrastructure, Micron's impressive growth could quickly stall, and the stock may be due for a deeper decline.

What Is Driving Palantir Stock?

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) stock rose 5.5% on Monday, November 9, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 2.3%. There was no announcement, earnings report or filing from the company around the move, and the rise came as Wall Street rebounded after a steep sell-off in global technology stocks the week before. Its latest earnings call came on November 2. So what ties Palantir to a rebound in tech stocks?

Palantir Fell With AI Stocks Before It Rose

Palantir sells an AI platform to companies and governments, and its stock had fallen alongside other AI stocks just before Monday's rise. It closed lower for seven straight sessions as AI stocks sold off, then fell another 9.7% on Thursday, November 5, three sessions after its third-quarter earnings call. It rose 3.5% the next day, so Monday's gain was its second in a row.

The business itself grew fast in its latest quarter. Revenue reached $2.31 billion in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 95.9% from a year earlier. Management said on the November 2 earnings call that U.S. commercial revenue from sales to American businesses grew 148% to $984 million, though the total value of new contracts the company signed rose a slower 6%.

Did Palantir Rise More Than Other Tech Stocks?

Mostly. Palantir's gain beat the 3.7% rise in XLK, the SPDR fund that tracks the technology sector, and the 2.7% gain in the Nasdaq Composite the same session. Among its peers, Snowflake rose as much as Palantir, while IBM slipped 0.2%. Palantir moved with technology stocks that day, and it rose more than the sector fund.

Palantir Stock Is Still Down Over Twelve Months

A rise this large is not rare for Palantir. The stock rose this much or more during 12 sessions in the prior 365 days, and its latest move of this size came two sessions earlier, in the other direction.

Even after two days of gains, the stock is down 19.1% since October 9, when it set its highest close of the past year. The S&P 500 posted a 3.3% fall over the same month. Over twelve months Palantir has lost 3.3%, while the S&P 500 returned 13.7%. Over six months the stock is still up 23.6%, a window that holds its lowest close of the past year, in June.

Palantir trades at 55.8 times its sales over the past twelve months, against 3.1 times for the S&P 500. On earnings the gap is narrower: 110.9 times against 21.8 times.

Palantir is expected to report its fourth-quarter 2026 results in February 2027. Its U.S. commercial revenue is the figure to watch.

Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks have been struggling lately, even though some names are still performing outstandingly well. Palantir Technologies (PLTR) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) have climbed to the top with another stellar quarter, but both stocks were recently caught up in the broader AI selloff. PLTR stock and AMD stock both fell 20% over a number of recent sessions, although they are now staging comebacks.

Investors have been questioning whether the enormous investments in AI and data-center infrastructure will generate sufficient enough returns to justify the spending. Concerns about tighter AI regulations and a possible slowdown in data-center construction have added to the pressure.

More News from Barchart

But the companies behind these two stocks are doing more than just getting by. They are thriving and raising the bar for growth. AMD is mounting an impressive comeback in the CPU market, taking market share from Intel (INTC) while expanding its presence in AI accelerators. Palantir, meanwhile, has shed its image as a government-only data analytics firm, with its U.S. commercial business outpacing U.S. government revenue for the first time in its most recent quarter.

Both of these companies are brimming with potential, but investors are paying increasingly high prices to own shares. At current valuations, one appears to have a considerably stronger case.

The Case for Palantir: Commercial AI Is Becoming a Powerful Growth Engine

Palantir creates software that helps governments and businesses make sense of large amounts of data and use that insight to make decisions. The Foundry platform serves commercial clients, while Gotham targets government and defense groups. The Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) also helps companies add AI models to their current operations. Instead of offering just another chatbot, Palantir wants to be the software that links AI to real business processes.

www.barchart.com

In the third quarter of 2026, Palantir's revenue skyrocketed 96% year-over-year (YOY) to $2.31 billion, with U.S. revenue jumping 119% YOY to $1.94 billion. Even more strikingly, commercial revenue shot up 113% YOY to $1.17 billion.

title: As Democrats Take Over Congress, Is Palantir Stock at Risk?
detail:
As Democrats Take Over Congress, Is Palantir Stock at Risk?
Jennifer Saibil, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:42 AM MST 4 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir Technologies(NASDAQ:PLTR) has been on fire, demonstrating accelerating growth as demand for its proprietary operational management systems increases.

Despite the relentless growth, Palantir stock is 23% off its October high. Wall Street has several worries about the company's future, including how well Palantir can compete in the age of agentic AI and how expensive the stock still is -- even after its recent slide, it trades at a lofty 112 times earnings and 56 times sales.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

However, there's a new concern that may eclipse any other ones. Palantir is a major U.S. defense contractor, supplying several government agencies and the military with sovereign AI services. Earlier this year, President Donald Trump asked for a $1.5 trillion budget for 2027, but Congress did not manage to pass a defense appropriations bill for next year during the session, and with a new Congress dominated by Democrats coming in January, that proposed budget isn't likely to be approved without significant revisions.

Image source: Getty Images.

Why Palantir is on fire

Palantir's original products were deliberately created for U.S. defense and intelligence agencies, and the company was backed by the CIA's venture capital arm.

It has more recently targeted commercial operations with its AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform), which connects a company's disparate data sets and unifies all of its AI apps and agents. This can give Palantir's clients a leg up on their competition and help them perform faster, more efficiently, and with greater accuracy in defining and reaching goals.

The company has been growing rapidly, and its new focus on commercial clients is generating incredible demand. In the third quarter, total revenue increased 96% year over year, driven by a 148% increase in U.S. commercial revenue.

It's also highly profitable, with a 62% adjusted operating margin and a 53% cash flow margin.

Why political headwinds may not derail its growth

The company's commercial revenue surpassed its government revenue for the first time in the third quarter, setting it up to thrive even if there are setbacks relating to government spending.

Palantir closed 212 deals worth at least $1 million in the quarter, including 107 worth at least $5 million and 64 worth at least $10 million. Total contract value (TCV) increased 6% from last year, but U.S. commercial TCV outpaced that, up 11%. That means Palantir is on track for higher revenue even if there is a slowdown in defense spending.

title: Forget Palantir? This IPO Candidate May Be the New "Autonomy Giant" in Defense.
detail:
Forget Palantir? This IPO Candidate May Be the New "Autonomy Giant" in Defense.
Rich Smith, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 9, 2026 at 5:50 PM MST 5 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

If you follow defense stocks -- and artificial intelligence (AI) -- you probably know about Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR). Privately owned for years before its September 2020 IPO, Palantir attracted significant investor interest even before it went public. Since Palantir went public, the stock is up 16-fold over barely six years, enough to make many investors into millionaires all on its own.

So what are the chances lightning like that could strike twice?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Double double trouble in defense

The chances may be better than you think, and amazing as it may sound, there's even a chance it may strike the very same kind of company: a popular defense stock focused on AI called Shield AI.

Much as Palantir was, Shield AI is a company that few people have heard of -- but it's been getting quite a lot of coverage lately and attracting the attention of defense investors. Just last week, defense news site Tectonic reported that Shield AI is raising $2.5 billion in cash at a $28.8 billion valuation to help pay for the acquisition of radar specialist Echodyne.

To put those numbers in context, Tectonic points out that as recently as March, Shield AI was valued at only $12.7 billion. So the valuation has doubled in the last eight months. What's more, as recently as 2025, Shield AI was worth only $5.3 billion. So in fact, the valuation has doubled twice in just the past year.

Introducing Shield AI

What is this defense contracting wunderkind? Well, according to its own website, Shield is a defense tech company with the ambitious goal of using AI-powered autonomy to guide "every military asset: aircraft, drones, ships, satellites, and submarines" by 2030.

Shield calls its own autonomy solution by the totally-not-terrifying name Hivemind -- it's the brain behind the company's V-Bat unmanned aerial vehicle (drone), its X-Bat vertical takeoff and landing fighter jet, and its Aechelon simulation platform for training both drone pilots and drone flight systems. (Aechelon also, incidentally, permits Shield's drones to operate without guidance from global positioning systems.)

As recently as a couple of months ago, I was writing about how Shield's software had become so capable that defense heavyweight L3Harris (NYSE: LHX) was enlisting its help in improving the performance of L3's VAMPIRE counter-drone rocket systems. Just one month later, Shield signed up another defense leader -- Italy's Leonardo -- to use Hivemind to power its Hivemind Proteus helicopter drone.
